_about: Published rules Quanta's readiness assessment applies. Every milestone names its source. Nothing here is Quanta's own opinion. Checked on 2026-09-25 against each primary source and at least one independent source; update the date and the entry when a source changes. A milestone with 'algorithms' applies only to sites using one of them (or whose algorithm cannot be read). 'in_force' marks a rule that already applies.

nist-ir-8547.title: IR 8547 (Initial Public Draft), Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography Standards
nist-ir-8547.where: Table 2 (signatures): ECDSA and RSA at 112-bit strength deprecated after 2030; ECDSA, EdDSA and RSA disallowed after 2035. Table 4 (key establishment): finite-field DH and MQV, elliptic-curve DH and MQV, and RSA at 112-bit strength deprecated after 2030; all disallowed after 2035. Quanta applies the 112-bit rows to RSA and finite-field DH, whose usual 2048-bit keys sit at 112 bits; elliptic-curve keys in use (P-256, X25519, Ed25519) are 128 bits or more.
nist-ir-8547.verification: Read from the NIST PDF. Dates confirmed by the EU roadmap (June 2025), which cites the same 2035 disallowance.

nist-sp-800-131a-r2.title: SP 800-131A Rev. 2, Transitioning the Use of Cryptographic Algorithms and Key Lengths
nist-sp-800-131a-r2.where: Table 1: three-key TDEA encryption disallowed after 31 December 2023; two-key TDEA encryption disallowed. Table 8: SHA-1 disallowed for digital signature generation. MD5 is not in the document's list of approved hash functions.

nist-sha1-retirement.title: NIST Transitioning Away from SHA-1 for All Applications
nist-sha1-retirement.where: SHA-1 to be phased out of all applications by 31 December 2030
nist-sha1-retirement.verification: Read from the NIST announcement of 15 December 2022; confirmed by FedScoop and Dark Reading.

nsa-cnsa-2.title: Commercial National Security Algorithm Suite 2.0 (Cybersecurity Advisory)
nsa-cnsa-2.where: Transition timeline: software and firmware signing exclusively CNSA 2.0 by 2030; web browsers, servers and cloud services by 2033; traditional networking equipment by 2030; operating systems by 2033; custom applications and legacy equipment updated or replaced by 2033. Applies to US National Security Systems.
nsa-cnsa-2.verification: NSA's host refuses automated download; the timeline was read from an archived copy of the NSA PDF (PP-22-1338, September 2022, version 1.0) and confirmed by Entrust (October 2022).

uk-ncsc-pqc.title: Timelines for migration to post-quantum cryptography
uk-ncsc-pqc.where: By 2028 discovery and an initial plan; by 2031 the highest-priority migration; by 2035 all systems, services and products migrated
uk-ncsc-pqc.verification: Read from the NCSC page; confirmed by The Quantum Insider (20 March 2025) and PQShield.

eu-pqc-roadmap.publisher: NIS Cooperation Group and European Commission
eu-pqc-roadmap.title: A Coordinated Implementation Roadmap for the Transition to Post-Quantum Cryptography
eu-pqc-roadmap.where: By 31 December 2026 first steps and national roadmaps; by 31 December 2030 high-risk use cases transitioned; by 31 December 2035 medium-risk use cases transitioned and low-risk use cases as far as feasible
eu-pqc-roadmap.verification: Read from the roadmap PDF (version 1.1); confirmed by Utimaco and PostQuantum.com.

nca-ncs-2-2025.title: National Cryptographic Standards NCS-2:2025 (public consultation draft)
nca-ncs-2-2025.where: Clause 2-5-5-1: a post-quantum cryptosystem must be used in hybrid with approved classical cryptosystems. Clause 2-5-1: ML-KEM-512 and ML-KEM-768 at the MODERATE level, ML-KEM-1024 at ADVANCED. The consultation closed on 25 December 2025; the draft sets no year.
nca-ncs-2-2025.verification: Read from the consultation PDF; the closing date is confirmed by Digital Policy Alert.

us-eo-14412.title: Executive Order 14412, Securing the Nation Against Advanced Cryptographic Attacks
us-eo-14412.where: US federal high-value assets and high-impact systems: post-quantum key establishment by 31 December 2030 and signatures by 31 December 2031
us-eo-14412.verification: Read from the White House text; confirmed by the American Presidency Project and Skadden.

openssl-3-5.title: OpenSSL 3.5 Series Release Notes
openssl-3-5.where: Default TLS key shares are X25519MLKEM768 and X25519: a Python program linked against OpenSSL 3.5 or later offers hybrid key exchange without code changes
openssl-3-5.verification: Read from the OpenSSL release notes; confirmed by Help Net Security (9 April 2025) and Phoronix.
